```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# For this analysis, we took the 225 children samples (1wpp) and the 245 mother samples (preg) available from Viterbi Gut. It represents 208 related pairs of mother and child. We performed StrainPhlan which is a reads based analysis that look at marker genes. 

# 1. Packages
```{r}
library(ape)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(writexl)
```

# 2. Get the taxonomy of the SGB from MetaPhlan tables
## 2.1 Extract taxonomy from MetaPhlan
```{r}
MetaPhlan_tax = read.delim("Supplementary_table3.txt", skip = 1)
# Extract taxonomy
MetaPhlan_tax <- str_split_fixed(MetaPhlan_tax$clade_name, "\\|[p,c,o,f,g,s,t]__", 8)
MetaPhlan_tax <- as.data.frame(MetaPhlan_tax)
MetaPhlan_tax[,1] <- str_remove(MetaPhlan_tax[,1], "k__")
# Keeping only the rows with the complete taxonomy
MetaPhlan_tax <- MetaPhlan_tax[-(which(MetaPhlan_tax[,8] == "")),]
# Changing colnames
colnames(MetaPhlan_tax) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class","Order","Family","Genus","Species", "SGB")
```

## 2.2 Get the most abundant SGB from StrainPhlan
```{r}
Clades_StrainPhlan = read.delim("Supplementary_table13.tsv")

Clades_StrainPhlan$Clade <- ifelse(
    grepl("t__", Clades_StrainPhlan$Clade),  # Check if 'Clade' starts with 't__'
    sub("t__", "", Clades_StrainPhlan$Clade), # Remove the 't__' if it exists
    Clades_StrainPhlan$Clade                    # Otherwise, keep the original value
  )

```

## 2.3 Merge taxonomy with clades
```{r}
Clades_StrainPhlan = left_join(Clades_StrainPhlan, MetaPhlan_tax, by = c("Clade" = "SGB"))

Clades_StrainPhlan <- Clades_StrainPhlan %>%
  mutate(Species = str_replace_all(Species, "_", " "))

rm(MetaPhlan_tax)
```


# 3. Get the list of SGB to test for strain sharing
```{r}
# Add a new column 'Potential_shared' to Clades_StrainPhlan
Clades_StrainPhlan$Potential_shared <- sapply(Clades_StrainPhlan$Samples, function(samples) {
  sample_list <- unlist(strsplit(samples, ",")) # Split the sample names by comma
  child_ids <- gsub("C1WST", "", grep("^C1WST", sample_list, value = TRUE)) # Extract VG_IDs by removing the prefixes ("C1WST" for child, "MPST" for mother)
  mother_ids <- gsub("MPST", "", grep("^MPST", sample_list, value = TRUE))
  shared_vg_ids <- intersect(child_ids, mother_ids) # Check if there is at least one matching VG_ID in both child and mother lists
  if (length(shared_vg_ids) > 0) { # Return 1 if there is a match, otherwise 0
    return(1)
  } else {
    return(0)
  }
})

# Create a new data frame with the list of SGB to test
SGB_to_test_df = Clades_StrainPhlan %>%
  filter(Potential_shared == 1)

# Then go on Curnagl and copy on my computer only the trees corresponding to the SGBs to test
rm(SGB_to_test_df)
```

# 4. Calculate normalised phylogenetic distances for all selected SGBs
```{r}
# Define the directory containing the tree files
tree_directory <- "Trees/directory"
# unzip the 78 trees

# List all files matching the pattern
tree_files <- list.files(path = tree_directory, pattern = "RAxML_bestTree.*\\.StrainPhlAn4\\.tre", full.names = TRUE)

# Extract tree names (without path)
tree_names <- gsub("RAxML_bestTree\\.|\\.StrainPhlAn4\\.tre", "", basename(tree_files))

# Import all trees into a list
trees_list <- lapply(tree_files, read.tree)

# Calculate total branch length for each tree
total_branch_lengths <- sapply(trees_list, function(tree) sum(tree$edge.length))

# Combine the tree names with their total branch lengths
branch_lengths_df <- data.frame(TreeName = tree_names, TotalBranchLength = total_branch_lengths)

# Normalize branch lengths and compute cophenetic distance matrix for each tree
normalized_trees <- lapply(trees_list, function(tree) {
  total_branch_length <- sum(tree$edge.length)  # Calculate total branch length
  tree$edge.length <- tree$edge.length / total_branch_length  # Normalize branch lengths
  dist_matrix <- cophenetic.phylo(tree)  # Compute cophenetic distance matrix
  list(tree = tree, dist_matrix = dist_matrix)  # Store both the tree and its distance matrix
})

  # Access the normalized tree and its distance matrix for the first tree
  first_normalized_tree <- normalized_trees[[1]]$tree
  first_dist_matrix <- normalized_trees[[1]]$dist_matrix

# Rename and clean the normalized_trees 
normalized_trees_df <- lapply(normalized_trees, function(tree_data) {
  dist_matrix <- tree_data$dist_matrix
  dist_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(as.matrix(dist_matrix))) # Convert distance matrix to a data frame
  colnames(dist_df) <- c("Strain1", "Strain2", "Distance") #renames the columns
  dist_df <- dist_df %>% # Filter rows: only keep unique strain comparisons and non-zero distances
    filter(as.character(Strain1) < as.character(Strain2)) %>%
    filter(Distance > 0)
  return(dist_df)
})

  # Access the processed distance data frame for the first tree
  first_normalized_trees_df <- normalized_trees_df[[1]]

# Extract SGB numbers from file names and combine data frames
dist_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(normalized_trees_df), function(i) {
  sgb_number <- sub(".*t__(SGB[0-9]+(?:_group)?)\\.StrainPhlAn4\\.tre", "\\1", basename(tree_files[i])) # Extract the SGB number with optional "_group" suffix
  df <- normalized_trees_df[[i]] # Add SGB identifier to the data frame
  df$Tree <- sgb_number  # Use the extracted SGB number (with or without _group)
  return(df)
}))

# Add taxonomy to the dist_df data frame
dist_df <- left_join(dist_df, Clades_StrainPhlan %>% 
                       select(Clade, Species), by = c("Tree" = "Clade"))

# Plot distance histograms for all trees
dist_df_wrapped <- dist_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Species = str_wrap(Species, width = 20))

distances_plot = ggplot(dist_df_wrapped, aes(x = Distance, fill = Species)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.0001, color = "black", alpha = 0.6, position = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~ Species, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5) +  # Creates a separate plot for each tree
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Phylogenetic distances across samples of all the potentially transmitted strains",
       x = "Normalized phylogenetic distances",
       y = "Frequency of pairs of samples") +
  theme(legend.position = "none", 
        plot.title = element_text(size = 24),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 20),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "italic")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.001, color = "red") + # Add vertical line
  xlim(0, 0.05)   # 👈 restricts x-axis to 0–0.05

# Remove unwanted objects
rm(tree_directory, tree_files, tree_names, trees_list, total_branch_lengths, branch_lengths_df, normalized_trees, normalized_trees_df, first_normalized_tree, first_dist_matrix, first_normalized_trees_df, distances_plot)
```

# 5. Strain sharing of all selected SGBs
```{r}
# Filter for strain pairs with distances less than 0.001 (based on what they used in Feehily et al, 2023)
shared_strains <- subset(dist_df, Distance < 0.001) # 1792 same strain events between all mothers and children

# Remove unnecessary objects
rm(dist_df)
```

# 6. Related vs Unrelated dyads - phylogenetic distances
## 6.1 Prep dataframes
```{r}
# Add a "Individual" and "Pairs" column to shared_strains data frame
shared_strains <- shared_strains %>%
  mutate(Individual = case_when(
    grepl("^MPST", Strain1) ~ "Mother",
    grepl("^C1WST", Strain1) ~ "Child",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_  # Default case if neither condition is true
  ))

shared_strains <- shared_strains %>%
  mutate(Individual2 = case_when(
    grepl("^MPST", Strain2) ~ "Mother",
    grepl("^C1WST", Strain2) ~ "Child",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_  # Default case if neither condition is true
  ))

shared_strains <- shared_strains %>%
  mutate(Pairs = ifelse((Individual == "Mother" & Individual2 == "Child") | 
                        (Individual == "Child" & Individual2 == "Mother"), 
                        1, 0))

# Add the Relationship variable (Related vs unrelated pairs)
  # Add VG_ID column by extracting the number and appending it to 'VG' (strain1)
  shared_strains <- shared_strains %>%
    mutate(VG_ID_1 = paste0("VG", gsub("^.*([0-9]{3}).*$", "\\1", Strain1)))
  
  # Add VG_ID column by extracting the number and appending it to 'VG' (strain2)
  shared_strains <- shared_strains %>%
    mutate(VG_ID_2 = paste0("VG", gsub("^.*([0-9]{3}).*$", "\\1", Strain2)))

shared_strains = shared_strains %>%
  mutate(Relationship = "")

shared_strains$Relationship[which(shared_strains$VG_ID_1 == shared_strains$VG_ID_2)] = "Related"
shared_strains$Relationship[which(shared_strains$VG_ID_1 != shared_strains$VG_ID_2)] = "Unrelated"

# Remove strains sharing between children only or between mothers only
shared_strains_all_pairs = shared_strains %>%
  filter(Pairs == 1)

table(shared_strains_all_pairs$Relationship) # 192 same strain events in related dyads and 420 same strain events in unrelated dyads

# Plot distances of shared strains
distance_plot = ggplot(shared_strains_all_pairs, aes(x = Distance, fill = Relationship)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.0001) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Related" = "#c6e2ff", "Unrelated" = "#ffe3c6")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Phylogenetic distances of same strains of related vs unrelated pairs",
       x = "Normalized Phylogenetic Distance",
       y = "Number of pairs of mother and child") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 20),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16),)

# Plot boxplots of distances of shared strains
wilcox.test(Distance ~ Relationship, data = shared_strains_all_pairs)


distance_plot_bp = ggplot(shared_strains_all_pairs, aes( x = Relationship, y = Distance, fill = Relationship)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Related" = "#c6e2ff", "Unrelated" = "#ffe3c6")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = NULL, # "Phylogenetic distances of same strains of related vs unrelated pairs"
       y = "Normalized Phylogenetic Distance") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16)) +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test",
                     label.x = 1.25,
                     label.y = max(shared_strains_all_pairs$Distance) * 1.1)

```

## 6.2 Calculate proportions of transmission in related dyads
```{r}
# We had in total in the sample data set 225 children samples and 245 mother samples, which represented 208 related dyads.
# For each child sample, a dyad can be formed with each mother sample. So, the total number of possible dyads is 225*245=55,125. The unrelated dyads are the total possible dyads minus the number of related dyads => Unrelated dyads=55,125−208=54917

# Proportions of the number of transmitted strains
table(shared_strains_all_pairs$Relationship) # 192 same strain events in related dyads and 420 same strain events in unrelated dyads
proportion_related = 192/208
proportion_unrelated = 420/54917

# Number of related dyads with at least 1 transmission event
shared_strains_all_pairs <- shared_strains_all_pairs %>%
  mutate(VG_ID = if_else(Relationship == "Related", VG_ID_1, NA_character_))
length(unique(shared_strains_all_pairs$VG_ID[!is.na(shared_strains_all_pairs$VG_ID)])) # 82/208 related pairs of mother and child share at least one strain

# Number of unrelated dyads with at least 1 transmission event - Create VG_ID variable
shared_strains_all_pairs <- shared_strains_all_pairs %>%
  mutate(VG_ID = if_else(Relationship == "Related", VG_ID_1, VG_ID_1))  # Ensure VG_ID is populated for both cases

unrelated_pairs_with_transmission <- shared_strains_all_pairs %>%
  filter(Relationship == "Unrelated") %>%
  distinct(VG_ID_1)  # Extract unique VG_IDs for unrelated pairs with transmission events

nrow(unrelated_pairs_with_transmission)  # 125/54917 unrelated pairs of mother and child share at least one strain

proportion_related_dyads = (82/208)*100 # 39.4%
proportion_unrelated_dyads = (125/54917)*100 # 0.22%

# Create a data frame with the data
proportions_df <- data.frame(
  Category = c("Related Pairs", "Unrelated Pairs"),
  Proportion = c(proportion_related_dyads, proportion_unrelated_dyads)
)
```

## 6.3 Frequency plots of shared strains between related and unrelated pairs
```{r}
# Create a frequency plot for the "Relationship" variable (= number of shared strain independently of proportions)
ggplot(shared_strains_all_pairs, aes(x = Relationship)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "grey", color = "black", width = 0.2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Frequency of Shared Strain in pairs of mother and child",
       x = "Shared Strain Category",
       y = "Frequency")

# Create a frequency plot for the "Relationship" variable by shared species (= number of shared strain independently of proportions)
ggplot(shared_strains_all_pairs, aes(x = Relationship, fill = Relationship)) +
  geom_bar(color = "black", width = 0.2) +  # Adjusted to fill color based on Relationship
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Related" = "red", "Unrelated" = "orange")) +  # Assign colors to categories
  facet_wrap(~ Species, scales = "free_y") +  # Creates a separate plot for each tree
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Frequency of Shared Strain in pairs of mother and child",
       x = "Shared Strain Category",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")  # Remove the legend
```

## 6.4 Proportions plots of shared strains between related and unrelated pairs
```{r}
# Statistics on shared strains between related vs unrelated pairs
# Number of shared strain events
shared_related <- 192  # Number of shared strains in related dyads
total_related <- 208   # Total number of related dyads

shared_unrelated <- 420  # Number of shared strains in unrelated dyads
total_unrelated <- 54917  # Total number of unrelated dyads

# Perform the proportion test
prop.test(c(shared_related, shared_unrelated), c(total_related, total_unrelated))

# Create a bar plot
proportion_plot = ggplot(proportions_df, aes(x = Category, y = Proportion, fill = Category)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "#bfbfbf", width = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Related Pairs" = "#c6e2ff", "Unrelated Pairs" = "#ffe3c6")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Related Pairs" = "Related",
                              "Unrelated Pairs" = "Unrelated")) +
  ylim(0, 45) +  # Set y-axis range for proportions
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = NULL, #"Proportion of pairs sharing a strain - related vs unrelated pairs"
       x = "Pairs Type",
       y = "Proportion of pairs sharing a strain") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14)) + 
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Proportion, 1), " %")), 
            vjust = -0.5,
            size = 5) +  
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 45, 
           label = paste("p <", format(2.2e-16, scientific = TRUE)), 
           size = 5)
```

## 6.5 Shared species within related pairs
```{r}
# Create a strain taxonomy column
shared_strains_all_pairs = shared_strains_all_pairs %>%
  mutate(Strain_Species = paste0(Species, " (", Tree, ")"))

# Create a frequency plot for the shared strains within related dyads
shared_strain_plot = shared_strains_all_pairs %>%
  filter(Relationship == "Related") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Strain_Species, Strain_Species, function(x) -length(x)))) +  # Reorder by frequency
    geom_bar(fill = "grey", color = "black") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, face="italic")) + # axis.title.x = element_blank()
    labs(title = NULL, # "Frequency of transmitted species within related pairs"
         x = "Transmitted strains within related pairs",
         y = "Number of tranmission events")

metadata = read.delim("VG_metadata.tsv")

# Get the shared strains for related pairs only
shared_strains_related_pairs <- shared_strains_all_pairs %>%
  filter(Relationship == "Related") %>%  # Keeps only related pairs
  left_join(metadata %>% select(VG_ID, classif, howborn_combined, howborn), by = c("VG_ID_1" = "VG_ID"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%  # Adds classif
    distinct() # remove duplicated rows

# Get the unique Trees (= strains) transmitted
tree_species_counts <- shared_strains_related_pairs %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Tree, Species) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Occurrences = n(), .groups = "drop")

num_non_unique <- tree_species_counts %>%
  dplyr::count(Species) %>%
  dplyr::filter(n > 1) %>%
  nrow()
print(num_non_unique)

num_unique <- tree_species_counts %>%
  summarise(num_unique = n_distinct(Species)) %>%
  pull(num_unique)
print(num_unique)

```

# 7. Nutritional status effect on strain sharing in the related pairs
## 7.1 Get metadata for the 208 pairs of mother and child
```{r}
# Get Metadata for the 208 pairs of mother and child analysed
metadata_filtered = metadata %>%
  filter((individual == "Mother" & Visit == "Inc") | 
         (individual == "Child" & Visit == "W1")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(SequencingID))  # Remove rows where SequencingID is NA

nrow(metadata_filtered %>% filter(individual == "Child")) # => 225 so all good
nrow(metadata_filtered %>% filter(individual == "Mother")) # => 245 so all good

  # Remove rows with unique VG_ID to keep only the pairs of mother and child
  metadata_pairs <- metadata_filtered %>%
    group_by(VG_ID) %>%
    filter(n() > 1) %>%
    ungroup()  # Optionally ungroup to avoid unintended grouping later

  
# Number of related dyads with at least 1 transmission event
  shared_strains_related_pairs_unique <- shared_strains_related_pairs %>%
  distinct(VG_ID, .keep_all = TRUE)  # Keep only one row per VG_ID
  
  # Create a table of observed frequencies
  observed_counts_prop <- table(shared_strains_related_pairs_unique$classif)
  
  # Proportion of pairs per nutritional group who share a strain
  proportions_classif_df <- metadata_pairs %>%
    filter(individual == "Mother") %>% 
    dplyr::count(classif) %>%  # Count occurrences of each 'classif' value for mothers
    mutate(proportion = n / sum(n))  %>% # Calculate proportions for each 'classif'
    mutate(Sharing_pairs_n = observed_counts_prop) %>%
    mutate(Sharing_pairs_p = (Sharing_pairs_n/82)*100) #we use 82 because there are 82 pairs for which there is at least 1 transmission event

```

## 7.2 Strain Transmission in related pairs in function of the nutritional group
### 7.2.1 Frequency of shared strains in related pairs
```{r}
# All transmission events
transmission_counts_all <- shared_strains_related_pairs %>%
  group_by(VG_ID) %>%  # Group by mother-child pair (VG_ID)
  dplyr::summarise(n_transmissions = n()) # Count the number of rows per pair

mean_n_transmission <- mean(transmission_counts_all$n_transmissions, na.rm = TRUE)
print(mean_n_transmission)  # 2.34 strains transmitted on average in a related pair

# Check if the number of transmitted strain is different between the nutritional groups
transmission_counts_byclassif <- shared_strains_related_pairs %>%
  group_by(VG_ID, classif) %>%  # Group by mother-child pair (VG_ID) and classif
  dplyr::summarise(n_transmissions = n(), .groups = "drop")  # Count transmissions and keep classif

avg_transmission_by_classif <- transmission_counts_byclassif %>%
  group_by(classif) %>%  # Group by classif
  summarise(avg_transmissions = mean(n_transmissions), .groups = "drop")  # Calculate mean

# Create a table of observed frequencies
transmission_counts_classif <- shared_strains_related_pairs %>% 
  group_by(classif) %>%  # Group by both mother-child pair and nutritional group
  dplyr::summarise(Sharing_events_n = n(), .groups = "drop")  # Count transmission events

# Calculate the expected number of transmissions per classification group
transmission_counts_classif <- transmission_counts_classif %>%
  left_join(proportions_classif_df, by = "classif") %>%
  mutate(Expected_sharing_event_n = (sum(Sharing_events_n) * Sharing_pairs_p)/100) %>%  # Total counts * expected proportion
  mutate(Expected_sharing_event_p = Sharing_pairs_p/100)

sum(transmission_counts_classif$Expected_sharing_event_n) # 192, so it's correct, it's the number of transmission events
sum(transmission_counts_classif$Expected_sharing_event_p) # 1, so it's correct, it's 100% of the related pairs sharing at least 1 strain

# Chi-square test
chi_test_fre <- chisq.test(transmission_counts_classif$Sharing_events_n, p = transmission_counts_classif$Expected_sharing_event_p)
print(chi_test_fre)
p_value = chi_test_fre$p.value

# Frequency of sharing events between nutritional groups
fre_shared_strain = ggplot(shared_strains_related_pairs, aes(x = classif, fill = classif)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Normally nourished" = "darkgoldenrod1", "Overnourished" = "coral1", "Undernourished" = "palegreen")) +
  geom_bar(color = "black", width = 0.2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Frequency of transmitted strain in related pairs in function of nutritional groups",
       x = "Nutritional group",
       y = "Frequency of transmitted strain") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = 85,  # Set y position inside the range
           label = paste("p =", signif(p_value, 3)), 
           size = 5)

# Frequency of sharing events between nutritional groups by species
fre_shared_strain_all = ggplot(shared_strains_related_pairs, aes(x = classif, fill = classif)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Normally nourished" = "darkgoldenrod1", "Overnourished" = "coral1", "Undernourished" = "palegreen")) +
  geom_bar(color = "black", width = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ Species) + #scales = "free_y"
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "Frequency of transmitted strain in related pairs in function of nutritional groups",
       x = "Nutritional group",
       y = "Frequency of transmitted strain") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

### 7.2.2 Proportion of shared strains in related pairs
```{r}
# Check if the proportion of related pairs having at least 1 transmitted strain is different between the nutritional groups
# Calculate the expected number of pairs sharing at least 1 transmission event per classification group
transmission_counts_classif <- transmission_counts_classif %>%
  mutate(Expected_sharing_pairs_n = (sum(Sharing_pairs_n) * proportion))   # Total counts * expected proportion

chi_test_prop <- chisq.test(transmission_counts_classif$Sharing_pairs_n, p = transmission_counts_classif$proportion)
print(chi_test_prop)
p_value = chi_test_prop$p.value

# Proportion of shared events in function of nutritional group
prop_shared_strain = ggplot(proportions_classif_df, aes(x = classif, y = Sharing_pairs_p, fill = classif)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", width = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Normally nourished" = "darkgoldenrod1", "Overnourished" = "coral1", "Undernourished" = "palegreen")) +
  #ylim(0, 40) +  # Set y-axis range for proportions
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Proportion of related pairs sharing at least one strain by nutritional group",
       x = "Nutritional group",
       y = "Percentage of pairs sharing at least one strain") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = 52,  # Set y position inside the range
           label = paste("p =", signif(p_value, 3)), 
           size = 5)  # Remove the legend

```

### 7.2.3 Top 5 transmitted species per nutritional group
```{r}
library(forcats)  # Needed for fct_reorder()

# Normally nourished
  top5_shared_normo = shared_strains_related_pairs %>%
    filter(classif == "Normally nourished") %>%
    dplyr::count(Species, sort = TRUE) %>%  # Count occurrences and sort in descending order
    top_n(5, n) # Select the top 5 species
  
  top5_normo = ggplot(top5_shared_normo, aes(x = fct_reorder(Species, n, .desc = TRUE), y = n)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "darkgoldenrod1", width = 0.2) +
    theme_minimal() + 
    labs(title = "Top 5 transmitted species in normally nourished pairs",
         x = "Species",
         y = "Transmission events") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face="italic"))  # angle = 45, hjust = 1,  Rotates x-axis labels

# Overnourished
  top5_shared_over = shared_strains_related_pairs %>%
    filter(classif == "Overnourished") %>%
    dplyr::count(Species, sort = TRUE) %>%  # Count occurrences and sort in descending order
    top_n(5, n) # Select the top 5 species
  
  top5_over = ggplot(top5_shared_over, aes(x = fct_reorder(Species, n, .desc = TRUE), y = n)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "coral1", width = 0.2) +
    theme_minimal() + 
    labs(title = "Top 5 transmitted species in overnourished pairs",
         x = "Species",
         y = "Transmission events") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face="italic"))  # angle = 45, hjust = 1,  Rotates x-axis labels

# Undernourished
  top5_shared_under = shared_strains_related_pairs %>%
    filter(classif == "Undernourished") %>%
    dplyr::count(Species, sort = TRUE) %>%  # Count occurrences and sort in descending order
    top_n(5, n) # Select the top 5 species
  
  top5_under = ggplot(top5_shared_under, aes(x = fct_reorder(Species, n, .desc = TRUE), y = n)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "palegreen", width = 0.2) +
    theme_minimal() + 
    labs(title = "Top 5 transmitted species in undernourished pairs",
         x = "Species",
         y = "Transmission events") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face="italic"))  # angle = 45, hjust = 1,  Rotates x-axis labels

```

## 7.3 Transmitted species unique to one nutritional group
```{r}
# Find species that are unique to a single nutritional group
unique_species_byclassif <- shared_strains_related_pairs %>%
  distinct(Species, classif) %>%  # Get unique combinations of Species and classif
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(n_classif = n()) %>%  # Count the number of unique nutritional groups per Species
  filter(n_classif == 1) %>%  # Keep only species found in one nutritional group
  pull(Species)  # Extract the Species names

# Filter the original dataframe for only the unique species
shared_strains_unique_byclassif <- shared_strains_related_pairs %>%
  filter(Species %in% unique_species_byclassif)

# Create a heatmap for visualization
  # Create a presence matrix for species vs classif
  species_matrix <- shared_strains_unique_byclassif %>%
    select(Species, classif) %>%
    mutate(value = 1) %>%  # Create a new column 'value' with 1 to represent presence
    pivot_wider(names_from = classif, values_from = value, 
                values_fn = list(value = max),  # Ensure 1, 1 becomes 1 (presence) instead of multiple 1's
                values_fill = list(value = 0)) %>%  # Replace missing values with 0
    column_to_rownames("Species")  # Set Species as row names
  
  species_matrix = as.matrix(species_matrix)
  
  # Generate heatmap
  library(ComplexHeatmap)
  heatmap_species <- Heatmap(species_matrix, 
                             name = "Presence",  # Title for the color scale
                             col = c("white", "grey42"),  # Colors: white for 0 (absence), blue for 1 (presence)
                             show_row_names = TRUE,  # Display row names (species)
                             show_column_names = TRUE,  # Display column names (nutritional groups)
                             cluster_rows = TRUE,  # Cluster rows (species)
                             cluster_columns = TRUE,  # Cluster columns (nutritional groups)
                             show_row_dend = FALSE,  # Do not show the row dendrogram
                             show_column_dend = FALSE,  # Do not show the column dendrogram
                             column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10, angle = 0),  # Make column names horizontal
                             column_names_rot = 0,  # Ensure column names are horizontal (angle 0)
                             row_names_gp = gpar(fontface = "italic", angle = 0),  # Make row names (species) italic
                             heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "Presence/Absence",  # Title for the legend
                                                         legend_direction = "vertical",  # Vertical legend
                                                         at = c(0, 1),  # Legend at 0 and 1
                                                         labels = c("Absent", "Present"))
  )
  # pdf("heatmap_species.pdf", width = 5, height = 8)  # Adjust width and height as needed
  # draw(heatmap_species, heatmap_legend_side = "bottom")
  # dev.off()
```

### 7.3.1 Common transmitted species between nutritional groups
```{r}
shared_strains_common <- anti_join(shared_strains_related_pairs, shared_strains_unique_byclassif, by = "Species")

shared_strains_common_O_NN = shared_strains_common %>%
  filter(classif %in% c("Overnourished", "Normally nourished")) %>%  # Keep only these classifications
  distinct(Species)  %>% # Get unique species
  filter(!Species %in% shared_strains_related_pairs$Species[shared_strains_related_pairs$classif == "Undernourished"]) # Remove species that also appear in "Undernourished"
num_unique_species <- nrow(shared_strains_common_O_NN)

shared_strains_common_O_U = shared_strains_common %>%
  filter(classif %in% c("Overnourished", "Undernourished")) %>%  # Keep only these classifications
  distinct(Species)  %>% # Get unique species
  filter(!Species %in% shared_strains_related_pairs$Species[shared_strains_related_pairs$classif == "Normally nourished"]) # Remove species that also appear in "Undernourished"
num_unique_species <- nrow(shared_strains_common_O_U)

shared_strains_common_NN_U = shared_strains_common %>%
  filter(classif %in% c("Normally nourished", "Undernourished")) %>%  # Keep only these classifications
  distinct(Species)  %>% # Get unique species
  filter(!Species %in% shared_strains_related_pairs$Species[shared_strains_related_pairs$classif == "Overnourished"]) # Remove species that also appear in "Undernourished"
num_unique_species <- nrow(shared_strains_common_NN_U)

shared_species_all <- shared_strains_related_pairs %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%  
  summarize(classif_count = n_distinct(classif)) %>%  # Count distinct classifications for each species
  filter(classif_count == 3)  # Keep only species appearing in all 3 classif
num_shared_species_all <- nrow(shared_species_all)
```
